nodes.title: SG-5 · Data-driven layered scene renderer and interactive object system
nodes.body:
Context: game/src holds engine/scene.ts (pure view/action logic), systems/*, a zod content schema (content/schema.ts) and a manifest loader with fallback (assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts). The Phaser side (frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) only reads state and renders nothing. Desired behavior: a generic engine under src/engine, src/scenes, src/entities and src/systems builds the bedroom from content definitions with nothing hardcoded in the scene class, renders ordered layers, preloads and validates assets with graceful fallback, supports interactive objects, dust and ambient light effects and scene transitions. Why: future AI cycles must add objects, characters and scenes by editing content and manifest only.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene definition, when it is built, then every object becomes an entity with no object id referenced in engine code
- Given objects on all six layers, when built, then display depth follows Background < Furniture < Interactive < Characters < Effects < UI Overlay
- Given a missing asset, when a scene is built, then a fallback texture is used and no exception is thrown
- Given an interactive object, when hovered, clicked, focused by keyboard or hidden by a visibility condition, then the correct highlight, label, event or removal occurs
- Given effects and a goto_scene event, when handled, then dust, ambient light and a fade transition run from content data


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/engine
- In scope: game/src/scenes
- In scope: game/src/entities
- In scope: game/src/systems
- In scope: game/src/assets/loaders
- In scope: content schema effects field
- In scope: Phaser scene adapter in frontend/src/phaser
- In scope: unit tests with Phaser mocked
- Out of scope: New pixel art
- Out of scope: React UI changes
- Out of scope: Backend/Go API changes
- Preserve: Existing getSceneView and performAction behavior
- Preserve: Existing manifest schema and loader exports
- Preserve: Existing typed event bus in frontend/src/phaser/events.ts


## Technical constraints
- Phaser 3.90 pinned in frontend; game/ package has no phaser dependency so engine code uses structural types
- Tests must mock Phaser, no browser
- Content validated by zod schemas


## Definition of done
- All requirements have Act and Verify units green
- Existing game and frontend unit tests still pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Pixel-art friendly rendering preserved
- No memory leaks: entities destroy their listeners


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene is built from content into entities on ordered layers
nodes.body:
Context: SceneDef objects carry asset, position, scale and layer (content/schema.ts layerSchema: background, furniture, objects, characters, effects, ui). No code creates display objects from them. Desired behavior: a layer-order module plus an entity class and generic buildScene create one entity per visible object, at the content position and scale, with depth from the layer. Expected: bedroom.yaml objects render without any per-object code. Why: adding an object is a content edit.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given objects on layers background to ui, when buildScene runs, then depths are strictly increasing in the order background, furniture, objects, characters, effects, ui
- Given an ObjectDef with position and scale, when built, then the display handle is placed at that position with that scale
- Given an object whose visibleWhen fails, when built, then no entity is created for it
- Given a new object appended to scene content, when built, then an entity exists without any engine code change


## Scope
- In scope: engine/layers.ts
- In scope: engine/renderContext.ts
- In scope: entities/SceneObject.ts
- In scope: scenes/buildScene.ts
- In scope: frontend WorldScene adapter
- Out of scope: Hover/click behavior
- Out of scope: Effects and transitions
- Preserve: getSceneView visibility logic in engine/scene.ts


## Technical constraints
- Reuse getSceneView for visibility
- No object ids hardcoded in engine code


## Definition of done
- buildScene exported and typed
- WorldScene delegates to buildScene


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Assets are preloaded, validated and fall back gracefully when missing
nodes.body:
Context: assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts already offers loadManifestWithFallback, checkAssetRefs and FALLBACK_ASSET_ID, but nothing turns a scene's asset refs into a preload plan. Desired behavior: a preload planner validates every object asset ref against the manifest, lists assets to load and returns a fallback texture key for any missing ref. Expected: a missing asset never throws and the object renders with the fallback. Why: broken content must not crash the game.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given refs present in the manifest, when planning, then the plan lists each asset once to load
- Given a ref absent from the manifest, when resolving, then the fallback texture key is returned and the ref is reported in missing
- Given a ref whose texture failed to load, when resolving, then the fallback key is returned without throwing
- Given duplicate refs, when planning, then each asset is loaded once


## Scope
- In scope: game/src/assets/loaders/preload.ts
- In scope: WorldScene preload() using the plan
- Out of scope: Changing manifest schema
- Preserve: checkAssetRefs and loadManifestWithFallback behavior


## Technical constraints
- Reuse checkAssetRefs and FALLBACK_ASSET_ID


## Definition of done
- Planner exported and used by WorldScene


## Non-functional requirements
- Avoid loading unreferenced assets


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Interactive objects support hover, label, click, actions and keyboard access
nodes.body:
Context: ObjectDef already carries interactionBounds, actions and visibleWhen; the typed bus defines objectHover and objectClick events. Desired behavior: SceneObject gets interaction bounds, hover tint plus name label, click emission, a contextual action list filtered by conditions, and keyboard focus cycling with Enter activation. Expected: hover and click events reach React through the existing phaserToReact bus. Why: acceptance requires accessible, clickable objects.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given pointerover, when it fires, then the object is tinted, its name label is shown and onHover(id) is called; on pointerout the tint clears, label hides and onHover(null) is called
- Given pointerdown, when it fires, then onClick(id) is called once
- Given actions with failing conditions, when listing, then only satisfied actions are returned
- Given focus order [a,b,c], when next is pressed from c, then focus wraps to a and Enter triggers a click on the focused object
- Given interactionBounds, when built, then setInteractive receives those bounds


## Scope
- In scope: entities/SceneObject.ts
- In scope: systems/interaction.ts
- In scope: WorldScene wiring to phaserToReact
- Out of scope: React ActionMenu changes
- Preserve: phaserToReact event names


## Technical constraints
- Objects without actions are not interactive


## Definition of done
- Events emitted through bus


## Non-functional requirements
- Keyboard accessibility


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Dust, ambient lighting and scene transitions are content-driven
nodes.body:
Context: sceneSchema has no effects field and nothing animates scene changes though the typed bus has transitionTo and the manifest holds effects/dust.svg. Desired behavior: add an optional effects array (types dust and ambientLight) to the scene schema, create effect entities on the effects layer, and run a fade-out, swap, fade-in transition. Expected: adding an effect or scene is a content edit. Why: atmosphere and scene changes without engine rewrites.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a scene with effects [{type:'dust'}], when built, then particles are added at the effects depth
- Given {type:'ambientLight',color,alpha}, when built, then an overlay with that color and alpha is added
- Given a scene without effects, when parsed, then effects defaults to an empty list and parsing still succeeds
- Given a transition request, when run, then fade out is called, then the swap callback, then fade in, in that order


## Scope
- In scope: content/schema.ts effects field
- In scope: entities/effects.ts
- In scope: engine/transition.ts
- In scope: bedroom.yaml effects entries
- In scope: WorldScene transitionTo handling
- Out of scope: New art
- Preserve: Existing scene parsing results for scenes without effects


## Technical constraints
- Effects use the dust asset id from the manifest


## Definition of done
- Effects and transition wired in WorldScene


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Export LAYER_ORDER as the six layer names, LAYER_DEPTH mapping background 0, furniture 100, objects 200, characters 300, effects 400, ui 500, and layerDepth(layer?: string) returning the mapped depth or the objects depth for undefined or unknown names.

Declare interface DisplayHandle with setPosition(x,y), setScale(s), setDepth(d), setOrigin(x,y), setVisible(v), setTint(color), clearTint(), setInteractive(bounds?), on(event:'pointerover'|'pointerout'|'pointerdown', cb), destroy(); declare RenderContext with addImage(textureKey,x,y): DisplayHandle, addLabel(text,x,y): DisplayHandle, hasTexture(key): boolean, addOverlay(color,alpha): DisplayHandle, addParticles(textureKey,count): DisplayHandle, fade(direction:'in'|'out', durationMs:number, done:()=>void): void.

steps.action: Create class WorldScene extends Phaser.Scene (key 'WorldScene') whose create() builds a RenderContext adapter over this.add.image/this.add.text, reads useGameStore.getState().state and runtime content scene, calls buildScene and stores the result; on SHUTDOWN call destroy().
